title: Modi opens 246 tribal projects worth Rs 3,000 crore on Birsa Munda's birth anniversary
dek: The Prime Minister joined the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas event in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, by video. The projects include Eklavya schools, PM-JANMAN centres and tribal museums in the north-east.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday inaugurated or laid the foundation stones of 246 projects for tribal communities worth about Rs 3,000 crore, at a Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, which he joined by video. The day marks the 151st birth anniversary of the tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda and closes a fortnight of events held across the country from 1 to 15 November.

Of the projects, 173 were inaugurated and 73 had their foundation stones laid, according to reports of the government's announcement. They are meant to strengthen education, health, livelihoods and village infrastructure in tribal areas.

## What was opened

The inaugurated projects include 38 Eklavya Model Residential Schools, the central government's boarding schools for tribal students, and 100 multi-purpose centres under PM-JANMAN, the mission for particularly vulnerable tribal groups, as well as other works under PM-JANMAN and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA), a programme for tribal-majority villages. They also include a new building for the Tribal Research Institute in Itanagar, Arunachal Pradesh, and the Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighter Museum in Aizawl, Mizoram.

Foundation stones were laid for 19 more Eklavya schools, 12 tribal multi-purpose marketing centres, meant to help tribal producers sell their goods, and 42 other PM-JANMAN and DAJGUA projects. Reports differ slightly on the breakdown, and the government's full list of projects by state had not been published by Sunday afternoon.

## What Modi said

Mr Modi spoke by video with beneficiaries from several states. A PM-JANMAN beneficiary from Yavatmal in Maharashtra described getting a permanent house and a toilet, and said life in the rainy season was no longer as hard. Mr Modi criticised earlier governments over the treatment of bamboo, saying the British had classified it as a tree, that the law should have been changed after independence, and that his government had changed it and given tribal communities full rights over bamboo.

## Background

India's Scheduled Tribes number about 10.4 crore, or 8.6% of the population, according to the 2011 Census. The government declared 15 November Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas in 2021. Eklavya schools are run by the Tribal Affairs Ministry, which aims to have one in every block with a tribal population of more than 50% and at least 20,000 tribal people.

West Bengal has a large tribal population, concentrated in Jhargram, Purulia, Bankura, Paschim Medinipur and the north Bengal districts of Jalpaiguri and Alipurduar. The reports of Sunday's announcement did not say which Bengal projects, if any, were in the list.

## What happens next

The Tribal Affairs Ministry is expected to publish the state-by-state list of projects. Gadchiroli, the venue, is a district long affected by Maoist violence, where the Centre and Maharashtra have been expanding roads and schools.
